scams.name: Hanoi Noi Bai Airport (HAN) Fake-Grab Driver Scam
scams.description: Hanoi's Noi Bai Airport (HAN) has the most-documented Vietnamese airport scam of 2024–2025: individuals pose as Grab or Be drivers, flash a phone screen that looks like a genuine rideshare app, and lead arriving tourists to unofficial cars that then charge 3–5x the legitimate fare. Community reports document the pattern: 'It's such a successful scam that's why Grab and Be set up personnel at the pickup zones' — but the scammers still operate in the arrivals hall itself. Travelers warn directly: 'These scammers will show you something on their phone that looks like a Grab screen. They are NOT Grab drivers.' One 2025 Hanoi victim account: 'Arrived at Hanoi Airport, fell into a fake Grab driver taxi scam. 100% my fault. My driver didn't have the app booking and the licence plate didn't match.' The legitimate fare from Noi Bai Airport to Hanoi Old Quarter is 350,000–400,000 VND (~$14–$16 USD) by licensed Mai Linh or Vina Sun taxi on the meter, or 230,000–300,000 VND via Grab / Be app pickup. Travelers give a universal rule: 'Never get a ride with a driver that approaches you in an airport, ever! In any country! It's a scam!' Community reports also document the common variant: drivers telling tourists they missed their bus or their hotel cancelled, and offering an 'alternative' ride at triple the rate. For older travellers arriving on a first-night Hanoi stay, the defence is absolute: (1) book a Grab or Be ride yourself at the airport Wi-Fi after you have your luggage; (2) verify the licence plate matches the app before entering; (3) if using a licensed taxi, use only Mai Linh (white taxis) or Vina Sun (green), and insist on the meter; (4) ignore every person in the arrivals hall offering 'taxi,' 'Grab,' or 'hotel transfer' — all are unauthorised; (5) the official Grab / Be pickup counter is past the car park — wait there, not in the arrivals terminal.
scams.avoidance: Book Grab or Be yourself on airport Wi-Fi AFTER you have your luggage — verify licence plate matches Use only Mai Linh (white) or Vina Sun (green) licensed taxis; insist on the meter Official fare to Old Quarter: 230,000–300,000 VND by app, 350,000–400,000 VND by licensed taxi Wait at the official Grab / Be pickup counter past the car park — not in the arrivals hall Ignore EVERY person in the arrivals hall offering 'taxi' or 'Grab' — all are unauthorised
scams.location: Noi Bai International Airport (HAN) arrivals hall and pickup zones, car park exit driveways, unauthorised pickup bays away from the official Grab/Be pickup counter

scams.name: Hanoi Taxi Meter Tampering & Route Skimming
scams.description: Even after avoiding the airport scam, Hanoi's street taxis present a second-layer problem: meter tampering, fake 'Mai Linh' and 'Vina Sun' copycats with nearly identical livery, and route skimming through extended back streets. Travelers are blunt: '95% of taxis in Hanoi are scams! Only use Mai Linh or Vina Sun or that new company that uses VinFast cars (Xanh SM).' Community reports document the classic pattern: 'taxi did not turn on meter, dropped me off at my destination and demanded an inflated cash price.' The copycat livery problem is severe. Real Mai Linh taxis are white with a green stripe; real Vina Sun are white with red/green branding. Copycats use nearly-identical logos (Mai Link, Vinasun copy) that tourists can't distinguish. One resident wrote: 'My mind can't comprehend how everything in tourist industry is designed to scam people here in Hanoi.' The new Xanh SM (VinFast electric taxi) is the 2025 community-recommended alternative — all-electric fleet, app-based, transparent fares. Community reports list taxi overcharging as the #1 first-day-scam pattern, with drivers charging 400,000 VND for rides that should cost 60,000 VND. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) use Grab or Be app for every ride — app-regulated fares and digital receipts; (2) if taking a street taxi, use only genuine Mai Linh, Vina Sun, or Xanh SM — verify the company phone number on the door matches the company website; (3) insist on the meter before the car moves; (4) typical Old Quarter rides: 40,000–100,000 VND; anything over 200,000 VND is overcharging; (5) photograph the taxi licence plate from the rear windscreen on entering; (6) for late-night returns from Bia Hoi Junction, pre-book Grab rather than hailing on the street.
scams.avoidance: Use Grab or Be app for every ride — app-regulated fares and digital receipts For street taxis, use ONLY Mai Linh (white, green stripe), Vina Sun, or Xanh SM (VinFast electric) Verify the company phone number on the door matches the real company website Insist on the meter running before the car moves Typical Old Quarter rides: 40,000–100,000 VND; anything over 200,000 VND is overcharging
scams.location: Old Quarter taxi ranks, Hoan Kiem Lake curbside hails, Temple of Literature exit, St. Joseph's Cathedral area, late-night return rides from Bia Hoi Junction

scams.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Shoe-Shine Aggressive Upcharge
scams.description: A specific Hanoi shoe-shine scam has been documented for over a decade and remains persistent in 2025. A 'shoe shiner' approaches, points at your shoe claiming it is damaged or needs urgent repair, and either forcefully removes your shoe to 'clean' or 'repair' it, or simply begins work before you can decline. The end price: 200,000–500,000 VND (~$8–$20 USD) for a 30-second shoe-shine that costs 30,000 VND from a legitimate operator. Community reports document the pattern: 'It's a common shoe scam in the big cities of Vietnam. They point at your shoe and while you're figuring out what they're saying, they've already started work.' The aggressive variant escalates to intimidation if you refuse to pay. The scammer may block your path, call companions, or claim you owe for 'cleaning' even if no work was actually done. Travelers note the important context: genuine shoe-shiners exist but work from fixed-location stalls with posted prices; anyone mobile in the Old Quarter targeting tourists with pointed-finger shoe 'damage' claims is running the scam. Community reports confirm the pattern extends to Ho Chi Minh City as well. For older travellers, the defence: (1) wear closed-toe shoes that don't attract shoe-shine attention; (2) if approached, keep walking without breaking stride, hands on pockets, 'không, cảm ơn' firmly; (3) NEVER let anyone touch your shoes or take them off; (4) if shoes are grabbed, walk to the nearest café or hotel lobby immediately — scammers rarely follow indoors; (5) if work has started and payment is demanded, pay 50,000 VND maximum and walk away — that's already above market rate for unsolicited work.
scams.avoidance: Never let anyone touch or take your shoes — keep walking without breaking stride Say 'không, cảm ơn' (no thank you) firmly and keep moving Only use genuine shoe-shiners at fixed-location stalls with posted prices If shoes are grabbed, walk to nearest café or hotel lobby — scammers rarely follow indoors If payment is demanded, pay 50,000 VND maximum — that's already above market for unsolicited work
scams.location: Hoan Kiem Lake perimeter, St. Joseph's Cathedral square, Old Quarter cafés along Ly Thai To, Train Street approach streets

scams.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Pickpockets & Hoan Kiem Lake Distraction Thefts
scams.description: Hanoi's pickpocket problem is more opportunistic than Barcelona's organised crews, but the Old Quarter's narrow streets and motorbike-dense crossings create specific risk moments. Community reports document Hoan Kiem Lake incidents and note that seasonal and returning travellers see the same patterns. 2025 reports place the Old Quarter pickpocket risk in the community baseline. The Hanoi-specific risk windows: (1) Hoan Kiem Lake perimeter during weekend night-market (Fri–Sun evenings) when pedestrian density peaks; (2) Train Street when the train approaches and crowds squeeze into café storefronts; (3) Bia Hoi Junction (Tạ Hiện, Lương Ngọc Quyến) during 7–11 PM beer-corner crowds; (4) motorbike bag snatching at intersections where pedestrians pause to cross (Hang Bac, Hang Dau). The motorbike-snatch variant is particularly dangerous for older travellers: a passing motorbike grabs a shoulder bag or phone being held while crossing, which can physically pull the victim into traffic. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) zipped crossbody bag worn in front during all Old Quarter walking; (2) never carry a phone in your hand while walking — motorbikes snatch them from sidewalks; (3) at Train Street, keep your phone in a zipped pocket and stay at the far side of any café storefront when the train passes; (4) at Bia Hoi Junction evenings, sit at an interior table rather than the open-sidewalk rows; (5) split valuables: passport + backup card in hotel safe, small cash + one card in front pocket for an evening; (6) for any theft, file report at Hanoi Tourist Police (46 Ly Thuong Kiet, +84 24 3822 2148) within 24 hours for insurance.
scams.avoidance: Wear zipped crossbody bag in front during all Old Quarter walking NEVER carry phone in hand while walking — motorbike-snatch risk is real At Train Street, stay at far side of café storefront when train passes At Bia Hoi Junction evenings, sit at interior tables not the open sidewalk File report at Hanoi Tourist Police (46 Ly Thuong Kiet, +84 24 3822 2148) within 24 hours
scams.location: Hoan Kiem Lake perimeter, Train Street narrow walkway, Bia Hoi Junction evening crowds, Old Quarter weekend-night-market on Hang Dao street, motorbike-dense intersections

scams.name: Hanoi Xe Om / 'Free Motorbike Tour' & City-Tour Overcharge
scams.description: The xe om (motorbike taxi) economy in Hanoi has two distinct scam genres targeting tourists. The first is the 'friendly motorbike tour' — a 'local' offers a city tour at a 'cheap' starting rate (400,000 VND) that escalates through 'gas stops,' 'bridge fees,' and route extensions to 1,500,000–2,500,000 VND by the end. One traveler wrote: 'First scam of the day: A friendly man offered me a motorcycle city tour for 400,000 VND.' The price then inflated. The second genre is the street-hail xe om with no meter: short rides that should cost 30,000–50,000 VND get quoted at 150,000–300,000 VND. Travelers describe the 'friendly local' pattern: 'scam on me within 10 seconds' — that's how quickly these interactions pivot from friendly to financial. Community reports document the cross-country pattern extending to places like Mũi Né. The proper Vietnamese motorbike-taxi economy runs through Grab (GrabBike) and Be (Be Bike) apps — app-regulated fares, GPS tracking, and digital receipts. Any xe om that approaches you unsolicited in the Old Quarter is operating outside the regulated system. For older travellers, the practical rule: (1) never accept a 'free tour' or 'friendly local motorbike ride' from someone approaching unsolicited; (2) use GrabBike or Be Bike app for short rides (30,000–50,000 VND typical); (3) for a proper guided motorbike city tour, book via a licensed operator (Vespa Adventures, Hanoi Backstreet Tours, Hanoi Vespa Tour) with fixed upfront pricing (€35–€60 for 3–4 hours); (4) for older travellers or those unfamiliar with Hanoi traffic, a walking tour via GetYourGuide or a small-group car tour is a safer alternative than motorbike; (5) helmet must be provided and worn — reject any ride without a helmet.
scams.avoidance: NEVER accept 'free tour' or 'friendly local' motorbike offers — all escalate to 1.5M+ VND Use GrabBike or Be Bike app for short rides — app-regulated fares, GPS tracked For guided motorbike tours, book via Vespa Adventures, Hanoi Backstreet Tours, or Hanoi Vespa Tour Older travellers: consider walking tours or small-group car tours rather than motorbike Reject any ride without a helmet for the passenger — legal requirement in Vietnam
scams.location: Old Quarter hotels where 'friendly locals' approach, Hoan Kiem Lake tourist stops, motorbike city-tour operators with inflated rates

scams.name: Hanoi Tinder / Overpriced Bar Extortion Scam
scams.description: Hanoi has a specific 2025 documented Tinder-honeypot scam that targets solo male travellers. A 2025 community investigation identified specific business addresses — typically a dodgy bar and a karaoke establishment — where the bill arrives at 15,000,000–50,000,000 VND (~$600–$2,000 USD) for a few drinks. The sequence: a match on Tinder or Bumble suggests a 'nice bar' she knows; the venue has no posted prices; drinks arrive in a bottle format at inflated 'hostess' rates; the bill is presented with bouncers blocking the exit; credit card fraud on the terminal adds another layer of cost. Community reports describe Hanoi Tinder as a scam hotspot, and travelers warn: 'Be careful in Vietnam, plenty of scammers on dating apps. Mostly they wanna lure you into an overpriced bar/karaoke venue.' First-person accounts describe bills of 20,000,000+ VND after 90 minutes of 'drinks.' For male travellers of any age using dating apps in Hanoi, the defence is absolute: (1) NEVER let a new date choose the venue — you pick, and you pick somewhere with posted prices and visible credit-card machine; (2) verify the venue name on Google Maps before going — if it has fewer than 20 reviews or mostly-5-star reviews with generic text, it's likely a scam venue; (3) never order drinks listed without prices; (4) never let 'hostesses' join the table — this is the trigger for premium-bottle charges; (5) if presented with an inflated bill, refuse to pay the unjustified amount, pay what the drinks were actually worth (30,000–80,000 VND each) and call Hanoi Tourist Police (46 Ly Thuong Kiet, +84 24 3822 2148); (6) community investigations explicitly name businesses to filter your Tinder matches against.
scams.avoidance: YOU pick the venue on any first date — never let the date choose Verify the venue on Google Maps — fewer than 20 reviews or generic 5-star text = scam venue Never order drinks listed without prices Never allow 'hostesses' to join the table — this triggers premium-bottle charges If trapped with inflated bill, pay honest rate (30K–80K VND/drink) and call Hanoi Tourist Police (+84 24 3822 2148)
scams.location: Old Town Hanoi bars off Ma May, Hang Buom, and Hang Be streets; specific venues flagged in 2025 community investigations; Tinder/Bumble date meetups at named copycat-bar addresses
